detail.longDescription: Below I created a function create_value_property which defines a set and get method and returns a property. How do I define this in such a way that the attributes val1 , val2 and val3 show as type V ( int in the example)? As it stands, custom.valn report type Any . I'm pretty sure it's because I'm using getattr and I don't know if I can specify the type that it will output. Is there a way to hint the property type? Python 3.14.6 IDE: VS Code Version 1.134.0 (Pylance) class EventHandler: def post_event(self, event: str): print(event) def create_value_property[V](name: str) -> property: def get(self) -> V: return getattr(self, f"_{name}") def set(self, value: V) -> None: prev_value = getattr(self, f"_{name}") if value == prev_value: return setattr(self, f"_{name}", value) self.event_handler.post_event(f"{name} value changed: {value}") return property(get, set) class Custom[V]: def __init__(self, val1: V, val2: V, val3: V) -> None: self._val1: V = val1 self._val2: V = val2 self._val3: V = val3 self.event_handler: EventHandler = EventHandler() val1: property = create_value_property('val1') val2: property = create_value_property('val2') val3: property = create_value_property('val3') custom = Custom[int](1,1,1) a = custom.val1 # a and custom.val1 report type Any custom.val1 = 2 custom.val2 = 3 custom.val3 = 4 I was able to figure out a middle ground. I was trying to avoid defining the same @setter for each property by using create_value_property . Instead I can do something like this and the typing works. I'm still curious if I can get the initial method working as it is much cleaner. def set_value[V](self, attr: V, value: V) -> None: if attr == value: return prev_val = attr attr = value self.event_handler.post_event(f"{attr} value changed: {value}") class Rev2[V]: def __init__(self, val1: V) -> None: self._val1: V = val1 self.event_handler: EventHandler = EventHandler() @property def val1(self) -> V: return self._val1 @val1.setter def val1(self, value: V) -> None: set_value(self, self._val1, value) An attempt with descriptors as suggested in the comments (with some functionality stripped out). Now the type inferred by the type checker for val1 is Unknown . class Prop[V]: def __set_name__(self, owner, name) -> None: self.name = name def __get__(self, instance, owner) -> V: return instance.__dict__.get(self.name) def __set__(self, instance, value) -> None: instance.__dict__[self.name] = value print(f"value set") class Rev3[V]: Val1 = Prop() rev3 = Rev3() rev3.Val1
